# Coaching places in 2027: a proposed rule

## What the rule does
Offer a coaching place to job seekers who have been unemployed for more than 10 and at most 15 months. This would offer 16% of seekers a place, within the budget of one place per five seekers; the remaining places can go to the seekers with the highest estimated gain in each region.

## What it is worth
On the 2025 and 2026 records, seekers decided this way would be employed within six months at a rate of 58.9% (95% interval 58.1% to 59.7%), against 57.5% under current practice: about 14 more seekers in work for every 1,000 registered. Giving places to the highest risk scores would do no better than current practice.

## Who it leaves out
Each region, women and men, and seekers with and without a disability are offered places at similar rates (the lowest region's rate is 91% of the highest). Seekers unemployed for more than 15 months (29% of all seekers, and half of Nijad's) are not offered a place by the rule: the pilot found coaching helps them less, and other services should serve them.

## Who reviews
Caseworkers review by hand the seekers at the edges of the band, seekers whose registration dates are uncertain, and seekers with a disability or living far from an office whom the rule leaves out (see the list attached).

## What would confirm it
A trial in which each new seeker is randomised to the rule or to current practice: about 18,000 seekers in each, roughly two years of registrations, with one look at the halfway point.
